answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s economic weight depend on a scarce, costly-to-renew credential rather than its claimed identity. For example, an agent locks a deposit in a vault and earns reputation only through completed trades that counterparties attest to; splitting into many identities does not multiply the deposit or trade history. A new vertex in the network starts with little influence, so the attacker must fund each identity and sustain real activity to gain trust. That ties a tempting nectar reward to capital at risk and operating costs.
